title: Give the seeker a goal
summary: Give the seeker a reason to look, then make the game fair for both teams.

steps.title: Points for seeing
steps.body:
Seekers score nothing yet. Press Check: it trains 4 hiders against 4 seekers for one generation and reports the best seeker's score. Every seeker scores 0, so evolution cannot tell a good seeker from a bad one, and it picks parents at random.

The `else` block runs for every player that is not a hider, which means the seeker. `agent.seesOpponent` is true while a player has the other one in sight.

Give the seeker `reward +1 * dt when agent.seesOpponent`: a point for every second it sees the hider.

check.message: The best seeker should score above 0.

hints: It has the same shape as the hider's first reward, with agent.seesOpponent.
Replace the comment in the else block with reward +1 * dt when agent.seesOpponent.

steps.title: Make it zero sum
steps.body:
In hide and seek every second goes to one side: the hider is either hidden or seen. Scored that way the game is zero sum. Whatever one team wins, the other loses, so no team can raise its score without beating the other.

Give the seeker the mirror image of the hider's penalty: lose a point for every second it cannot see the hider. Careful with prep. The seeker is frozen and blind then, so it should not lose points it had no chance to win. `agent.prep` is true during prep.

Add `reward -1 * dt when not agent.prep and not agent.seesOpponent`. The check adds up both teams' points from the test match and expects exactly 0.

check.message: The hider's and the seeker's points should add up to 0.

hints: not turns true into false and false into true. and joins two conditions.
Add reward -1 * dt when not agent.prep and not agent.seesOpponent under the seeker's reward.

steps.title: Eyes that remember
steps.body:
The rays of `hideseek-starter` only measure distance, so a wall and a box look the same. And once the hider slips out of sight, the seeker has no idea where it went.

`hideseek-standard` sees more. Its sixteen rays also tell walls, boxes and players apart. It knows whether it holds a box and how much time is left, and it keeps the direction where it last saw the other player. It sees the nearest ramp too, like the starter brain. That makes 61 inputs instead of 17.

Change the brain line to `brain hideseek-standard`. Both teams use the brain the script names.
hints: The brain line picks the network and its inputs.
Change brain hideseek-starter to brain hideseek-standard.
